reviews.text: Good morning, I wanted to thank Dr. Cortesi and his assistant who, on the night of Sunday, October 11th, took in my husband and I, who were distraught over the death of our sweet cat. They were incredibly kind, empathetic, and professional. Thank you so much, from the bottom of my heart.

A terrible experience!
The doctor is a fisherman in troubled waters who only exaggerates to make a profit, and I can prove it. Even worse, he lied knowing he was lying!
My wife and I knew full well what was wrong with our friend.
End of story: Even though he told us he had made a great recovery, when we arrived, we found him dead and cold. It happened right after we left at 12:30 PM and returned to pick him up at 3:30 PM. We had serious doubts about what he had told us half an hour earlier—that he had made a great recovery. In fact, he denied everything, and was very evasive from the beginning, emphasizing his dubious professionalism in the matter.
Don't bring your pets there if you truly love them!

I went to this clinic overnight for my rabbit last summer and had a great experience, but last night when I called back, a not very empathetic lady on the phone told me to go elsewhere on Nomentana, and when I asked where she was referring, I was told to use GPS. Congratulations, you've lost a client.
They made my cat die
Terrible experience. A 3-minute visit to my cat for an excessive cost. I went elsewhere and got everything, another treatment at a much lower cost.

The clinic is excellently equipped, open 24/7, and capable of handling any emergency. I used their services for over a month for our dog/kitten, who sadly passed away due to a serious illness. We received special care from Dr. Francesco Ceccaroni, a truly knowledgeable physician. During the painful final diagnosis, he was there for us with great integrity, professionalism, and exceptional humanity. A heartfelt thank you to him, Dr. Pavone, and the entire staff.

My sister had a very bad experience. She brought her 12-year-old dog there. They turned him around like a little dog. He went in fine, came out dead. I don't like this clinic at all. For example, I got along very well with the bourgeois clinic. They are very serious in their profession.

Some time ago, we brought our dog, Totò, a Bichon Havanese, to this clinic. He was very ill with advanced sepsis. Many vets couldn't tell us what he had, until we found this clinic that truly took care of our dog. They were not only affectionate with him, but also very kind and competent. A huge thank you to Dr. Ceccaroni and his entire staff for saving Totò! We will be forever grateful.
That veterinary clinic assigned me to have my dog ​​cremated, and it was the worst experience; besides how badly she was suffering.

If you bring your pet here, you should be aware that communication from the staff, and particularly from the facility's medical director, is intentionally unclear, to push people toward treatments that generate profit for the clinic itself—or at least that was my overall impression.
My expectation is that when faced with an animal in critical condition, a plan can be made calmly with a good-faith veterinarian, evaluating the risks, possible realistic success rates, and the costs of a given treatment. At this facility, that's not the case. It was very unfortunate, in addition to the pain of seeing my cat in pain, to feel like I had to defend myself from various attempts at psychological manipulation to accept a series of very expensive tests and treatments, with very little chance of success. I'm giving it two stars instead of one because some staff members (including the doctor who performs the ultrasounds and Dr. Pavone) are good people who try to do their job well, but I believe the problem lies precisely with the corporate culture created by the manager—I believe his name is Ceccaroni. If you need to come for an emergency, that's fine, but try to avoid hospitalization if possible or at least minimize your stay. Especially if you're in critical situations, being cared for by someone who does this work with integrity and compassion makes a huge difference.

I would like to thank Veterinarian Dr. CORTESI, who one evening last week was incredibly kind and attentive in advising us on our dog, who was very ill. He was attentive, thorough, empathetic, and incredibly clear! Together with Technician Giulia, he gave the best advice for our dog, who is still in a bad way (and there's not much more that can be done because he's old), but at least he's still with us. Thank you so much.

I dealt with them years ago, I came across their page and I can't help but write a review. They're excellent, very humane and professional, but (sorry for the harsh words) they basically killed my dog ​​by misdiagnosing them. Unfortunately, to err is human. In general, from experience, I recommend always getting a second or even third opinion from other vets for delicate situations. They're great because they're also open late at night for emergencies.

I visited the clinic because my dog ​​had gastroenteritis. She had been having diarrhea for two days, wasn't eating, only drinking water occasionally, and was constantly trembling, refusing to move because of the pain (unfortunately, these episodes happen repeatedly because she's very sensitive to changes in food, and since we were on vacation, she had eaten a different type of food, but every time she goes to the vet they give her probiotics and injections that help her recover immediately). They refused to give her anything, only an edible intestinal paste that had no effect, and wanted to keep her hospitalized! I refused because I didn't feel confident in the treatment, and thankfully the next day we flew back to Switzerland (with my dog ​​in great pain and unable to move) and she immediately started a probiotic treatment with immediate effect! Now, thank God, she's better, and I'm glad I didn't leave her hospitalized because they had no empathy for an animal in pain.
Always kind, competent and available.

The staff were friendly and helpful, always open, and the vet was knowledgeable and friendly. There was a bit of a wait because it was busy, but they were very professional and served our furry friends. Highly recommended.
Unfortunately, I had to go there for the euthanasia of my furry friend but, in that sad moment, I found a doctor who was not only competent, but also very kind and understanding.

The most competent and compassionate veterinarian I've ever met! He and his staff treated my Cane Corso, Duncan, with incredible professionalism and love. Duncan underwent prosthetic surgery on his hind leg, which he practically no longer used because it was constantly hanging. Now he's a happy, pain-free dog, thanks to Dr. Ceccaroni and his staff, who took on this enormous responsibility.

I was lucky to find this vet! He was honest, transparent, and did everything possible to keep us from spending a fortune.

A true professional! His kindness was incredible.

I was impressed by his ability to explain things clearly and simply. He answered all my questions and made my dog ​​feel at ease. I highly recommend him!

Thank you so much, everyone.
I didn't know this clinic, unfortunately I know it for an emergency room, and honestly I strongly advise against it. Negative experience.

I wanted to thank Dr. Lucia for her promptness and the thoroughness with which she took care of my hospitalized dog, along with Dr. Ceccaroni who was always present. Thanks also to the staff, Sara, Simona, and Giulia, who were always available. I'm sure I've forgotten someone.
All well done, I wanted to thank the terrifying Lucia for her timely intervention with my dog ​​and her scrupulousness and also thanks to Doctor Ceccaroni

I want to sincerely thank all the doctors at the clinic for their compassion, availability, and professionalism every single day.
For weeks, they helped me almost every morning to give my cat Moony her injections, with patience and care, without ever asking for anything in return.
In a very difficult time, I never felt alone: ​​I found people who, even before being veterinarians, were present, supportive, and deeply human.
It is also thanks to them that Moony is well today and returning to her life.
I will never forget what you have done for us.
Thank you so much, from the bottom of my heart.

A huge positive feed to all of you. Especially to Drs. Francesca Costanzo, Arianna D'Arcone, Pavone, and Dr. Ceccaroni. I urgently brought my Toby in for a tumor on his back that had unfortunately ruptured. Toby is a 15-year-old dog with multiple medical conditions, including serious heart problems. We were greeted by Sara, the nurse, a true delight to say the least—kind, affable, and empathetic. Immediately afterward, Dr. Arianna took care of Toby and explained the situation to me thoroughly and clearly. Meanwhile, Dr. Pavone arrived, followed by Dr. Costanzo. We returned in the afternoon for the echocardiogram. Toby made everyone sweat because he's so restless. Afterward, Dr. Ceccaroni greeted us, also invaluable for his expertise and courtesy. We mutually decided that surgery was the only possible way to try to save him. On the day of the surgery, we went back to the clinic, and everyone was there, and as usual, they welcomed us with unparalleled empathy. I, terrified, was comforted by Drs. Francesca and Arianna, who let me stay with Toby until he was sedated. After the surgery, they promptly called me to tell me everything had gone well. I went to pick him up and took him home. I called a couple of times with concerns about the wound, and everyone who answered was incredibly kind and helpful. At the post-op check-up a week later, I found them both again, welcoming us with smiles and so much patience, given Toby's agitation (he's very calm with them). There... I can't thank you all enough for what you've done! You were unparalleled. I've met you on other occasions and with other beloved furry friends of mine, and your comfort for me was already immense. But this time, you outdid yourself! A big hug and a huge thank you from me and Toby!!!

Terrible is an understatement. I went there to give my cat a simple enema, and they threw in unnecessary tests to make money. The estimate for simply having my cat evacuated was over €500, but it was cut in half because I refused to take any more unnecessary tests. Finally, they didn't even do the enema, and I have to do it myself at home. Shame on you, you're exploiting people's love for animals just to make money. Absolutely avoid them.

There is zero otherwise they deserve what they deserve, today begins a new year and my wish for everyone is to never find themselves having to or being forced (because there is no place for hospitalization in other clinics) to go to this facility.... zero empathy, they only try to continue the hospitalization or intensive care to make money, they are not worthy of being called doctors, my Stella is no longer here but you who are reading please do not bring your friends to this facility, you still have time

They don't even deserve a single star. They only think about making money and taking advantage of our moment of fragility! A day in the hospital (unnecessary) but they make you believe they are the saviors of the country 500 euros. The dog drank the water from the puddle as soon as he came out because he was so thirsty! DON'T GO THERE FOR THE SAFETY OF YOUR FURRY CAT

Absurd!!!
I arrived with my dog ​​late at night because he cried if I touched his paw!
The doctor on duty that night couldn't tell me or do anything! On top of charging me 100 euros for a visit, NOTHING, she also wanted to give me a nonsensical medicine that cost another 100 euros!!
Not to mention the doctor sounded like she was on drugs from the way she spoke! I've always had a good experience at this clinic, with other doctors who were ABSOLUTELY much more efficient.
Good evening, I was here today for the first time and I brought my dog. I can only say that Dr. Ceccaroni is a truly capable, kind, and humble person. Thank you, thank you very much.

A terrifying experience.
We went to the clinic on the advice of veterinarian Policastro to have a parvo exam (fecal test) and a complete blood count, as our kitten was vomiting water and pooping 7-8 times a day, symptoms the veterinarian said were potentially dangerous.
Once we arrived at the clinic, we were handed over to a young veterinarian who introduced herself as Elvira. After informing her of the issues, she began examining her. She then began formalizing the possible diagnosis in a very academic manner, stating that there could be risks to the kitten's life. She proposed hospitalization for tests and IVs to hydrate her, and in a very calm manner, began compiling a quote (€90 per day for hospitalization plus ultrasound, blood gases, and complete blood count). Concerned and surprised, my wife and I consulted and decided not to hospitalize her; the kitten's clinical condition did not warrant hospitalization.
At our insistence, Dr. Elvira called the Policastro veterinarian, who in turn recommended hospitalization (I saw a certain complicity), all the more reason to take her home. The whole thing cost us €70 for the visit, in addition to the great worry. Our impression is that the focus was more on making money than the kitten's well-being.
Today, our kitten is doing very well, lively, and her symptoms have disappeared. We turned to another very good and reliable veterinarian. Our experience with the San Giovanni clinic was negative, and I discourage anyone from bringing their pet there. Love, ethics, and acting with good faith are probably not the priority; replenishing the coffers certainly is. Dr. Elvira can still redeem herself; she's young and probably capable of saving herself while she can.

Extremely disappointing and worrying experience

My experience with this veterinarian was unfortunately very negative.
In July, my Persian cat began sneezing and bleeding from his nose. The doctor examined him in the emergency room and prescribed a seven-day course of antibiotics, combined with a nasal spray. Initially, the cat seemed to be doing better, and we thought the problem was resolved.

In September, however, the symptoms returned, with even more heavy bleeding. The veterinarian simply recommended the nasal spray again, pending the results of the manual platelet count and coagulation test, both of which later proved normal. Despite the obvious deterioration and my repeated alarms, my concerns were dismissed as "paranoia," and I was told that "it's normal for a Persian cat to have nasal discharge"—as if I didn't know my pet after 11 years of living together.

She had me undergo two ultrasounds, one abdominal and one cardiac, which were completely useless in addressing the underlying problem, only wasting my time and money.

Eventually, faced with renewed and profuse bleeding, I was forced to consult another clinic, where—thanks to a timely assessment of the severity of the situation—I was recommended a rhinoscopy with histological sampling, and a diagnosis of severe purulent infectious rhinitis was made. My cat is now undergoing heavy antibiotic and corticosteroid therapy for a month.

If I had continued to trust the superficial judgment of my previous veterinarian, I dare not imagine the consequences.

Such a lazy and hasty attitude in the face of such obvious symptoms is unacceptable for anyone who works in animal health.

On May 27th, after a long illness (intestinal lymphoma), I had my beloved Theo (a 10-year-old tabby) put down at this clinic. Dr. Ceccaroni was magnificent throughout the entire course of his illness. And at the worst moment, when you know you have to let go of someone you love but are suffering terribly… he gave me a beautiful gift: Momo, a sweet black kitten (see photo), abandoned in front of the clinic with four other siblings.

Avoid this clinic. The staff is unprofessional, unprepared to say the least (except in a couple of cases), and persistent attempts to hospitalize them are both unnecessary and costly. It was a terrible experience, with my dying dog being cared for on a dirty floor, while the room was being used for other tests. The staff was incapable of inserting a butterfly tube under the skin for a saline drip. If your pet is terminally ill, avoid it; you risk never being able to say goodbye to them because they are hospitalized solely for financial reasons.

Last week, Bignè, my 4-year-old cat, was hospitalized and then operated on due to a 1.5 cm bladder stone. Yesterday, a week later, we had a checkup, and he passed with flying colors! In addition to the entire staff, I sincerely thank Dr. Lucia Pavone, who handled the entire diagnostic process and post-operative care with great expertise and compassion—managing my furry friend, who was certainly not easy to manage, with a smile!—and Dr. Francesca Costanzo, who performed the surgery with exceptional skill. The stitches looked like they were done by a plastic surgeon! Thank you so much!

One Sunday morning in August, we brought our two-year-old cat with a serious chest wound she'd sustained from a blunt object while escaping an attack from a neighbor's cat.
Astra underwent surgery and survived, but then, after some ups and downs, nine days after the operation, she suffered a severe respiratory crisis and died. She was treated with excellent care, and everything that might be necessary/helpful was agreed upon.
We made it clear that we were against aggressive treatment and, above all, that we should be notified immediately if the cat was in pain, and so we did.
Astra was young and lively, and I will always remember her leaping, twisting, five feet off the ground around wind-blown leaves; He had a great zest for life, which, combined with the skills and professionalism of this facility, we hoped would be enough... it didn't happen that way, but I know that without raising any false hopes, without bowing to the owners (often directed more at the animals than at them), everything possible was done.

Thank you

I thank the girls at the veterinary clinic. Arianna, Sara and the other angel whose name I don't remember for being close to me both medically and above all humanly in the worst moment of my life. In the misfortune I met three wonderful women. My little good bridge I will never forget you.... I will always love you.

I'll give it one star, otherwise I can't write a review. When they provide estimates, they specify that none of the tests or labs can be done on-site and that you have to wait for the day when the sonographer, radiographer, etc., are there. While waiting for that fateful day, they don't tell the client that the cat must remain there for observation (i.e., locked in a cage meowing without food because he can be perfectly fine at home), thus multiplying the hospital stay infinitely. So the more money they fleece from you, the better it is for them!!! Let's leave aside the cost of each test; the attempt to be very scientific in the explanations is quite useless and touching, so the bill is justified. I assume I know what an ultrasound and an X-ray are, and I don't understand why they did five of them. Oh, I paid an astronomical amount without having solved anything; the cat was vomiting before and is vomiting now. To solve the problem, perhaps a gastroscopy will be needed, which could turn into a surgical operation with a team of stellar doctors, and it might cost 500 or 1000 euros, or whatever, so everyone is good at being a doctor. I understand why people abandon animals because PLACES LIKE THIS exist.

A friend recommended the clinic to me; I went there for my dachshund, Goliath. I spoke with Dr. Piccininno and was very impressed with his professionalism, courtesy, and attention to detail. He reassured me and explained the problem clearly and simply. Goliath is doing better. Thank you both!

After the welcome I received from the princess doctors, I noticed their lack of experience and lack of humane treatment for the dog, but their terrible experience, unfortunately, only became apparent later. Their deceptive words, full of money-making slogans, are deceptive, and their appearances are just smoke and mirrors. Exorbitant costs!
And alas, I'm the only one who pays for losing my Margarita...
Because their fee is already in their account!!! But I believe in God and there will be justice!!!
Meanwhile, shame on you!!!
Kind and helpful, they solved my dog's problem in a few minutes. Thank you.

Excellent clinic in the San Giovanni area, with knowledgeable and welcoming staff. They took care of my beloved cocker spaniel Brando with kindness and professionalism. Dr. Cacciaroni is very knowledgeable, professional, and helpful. Thank you ❤️

INHUMANE
I will never forgive the fact that, while my little dog was dying, the doctor filled out my personal information instead of examining him.

I arrived urgently with my little dog crumpled in my arms, and they let me in right away. But instead of examining him, the doctor sat down at the computer, typing and collecting my information as if I were about to run away like a thief.
While I was stunned to see if this paradoxical situation was real, and while I felt like an idiot for being forced to reel off my tax code, instead of comforting him and giving him a final caress and a kiss and saying a fitting goodbye to my beloved little dog, he died without anyone doing a thing: listening to his heart, looking at the color of his gums, nothing! They didn't even touch him!
When I told the doctor, "Look, he's pooping," he finally stood up, approached my dog, and touched him for the first time since I'd been there (!) He was impatient and nervous, and exclaimed, "He's dead!" as if I'd been so stupid as to bring him a dog that was already dead.

Then I yelled, "He's dead now!"

Finally, the doctor seemed to have suddenly awakened from his apathy and rushed him, now lifeless and inert, to intensive care.

My little dog recovered, but shortly afterward he passed away again, and further attempts to revive him were futile.

I was finally able to say goodbye to my dog ​​only when he was already dead, his eyes dull and lacking the light and spark of life.
Kind and very good
Everyone is super helpful and very kind, thank you

Betty and I thank you with all our hearts. Competent and human professionals, qualities that aren't taken for granted, but with you, they're guaranteed. You've given us more time together, and for that, we will be forever grateful.

As always, I'm satisfied with the treatment I received at this clinic. We've been treated here forever and have never had any problems.
My three cats now trust the doctors just as much as we do, for their skill and the gentle way they treat them.
Entrusting my pets to Dr. Ceccaroni is a guarantee for me, thanks to his expertise, experience, honesty, and helpfulness.
All the staff have always been very friendly, compassionate, and ready to answer any questions.
Seeing is believing :)

I came because my cat had been sick for days. When I arrived, they treated me extremely kindly, and I didn't have to wait. The staff is undoubtedly highly qualified, and the environment is comfortable and pleasant. I recommend anyone to visit this facility if they need it.
They are now a guarantee, they have taken care of all my cats and they were fantastic... they are super helpful, precise, professional but above all human

I brought my parents' cat for a problem, and they were all super kind and did everything they could to help me.
I highly recommend them.

Professionalism, expertise, and great humanity—things that are far from guaranteed. Thank you, Dr. Marzia Radicchi. When you find yourself having to rely on someone, finding a professional like her is a game-changer. I wish I'd met her sooner.

In August, I went to the San Giovanni clinic (where I'd been before and found very kind staff and competent doctors) because my 13-year-old dog hadn't eaten all day (trying only once and vomiting shortly afterward), but above all because she was having spasms and skin contractions around her chest, symptoms that, despite the dog having had gastritis and intestinal problems throughout her life, she had never exhibited. I arrived at 7:30 in the morning and was seen by a doctor who, probably tired from the end of her shift, gave her a very superficial examination (she didn't even take her temperature) and discharged her with a diagnosis of gastritis (€120 because she was in the emergency room for this "visit" and a small injection of I don't remember what medication to treat this presumed gastritis). Moral of the story: the dog isn't improving and continues to feel sick, so much so that in the afternoon I called the clinic to ask if I should take her back for a check-up. I was told no, to give her Buscopan and wait. The next day, just to be on the safe side, I took her to another clinic, and the dog had nothing less than a PYOMETRA, with discharge from the vulva (which would have been visible if only she had been examined properly). If I had trusted them and waited as I was told, I probably wouldn't have been able to catch her in time. It's a shame because, as I said, I'd had good experiences with them in the past, but at this point, I highly recommend looking at other clinics in the area!

RUN AWAY!!!!! I took my cat in for a urinary tract obstruction. He was catheterized for 48 hours and discharged with an eye infection (because the clinic was too dirty), blood clots when he urinated, and I immediately noticed that his urine smelled bad. I took him to another vet who immediately did a urine culture, and days later, staphylococcus was found in his urine!!!!!

HORRIBLE!!!! If you love your pets, stay away from this clinic!!!! I took my cat in for cystitis and in three seconds they told me, "The cat is dying because it's blocked, we need to put in a catheter right away, he'll have to stay here for three days, and we're sorry for this expensive diagnosis." While I was trying to stay calm,
they took him away without even letting me say goodbye because they were in a hurry to get my deposit. When I returned the following days, I noticed that my cat's fur smelled of smoke, and the other owners of the other hospitalized pets were complaining of the same thing. My cat was discharged with a pus abscess on his penis, he was urinating blood, and he had severe conjunctivitis. I called them as soon as I got home after being discharged and they told me that pus from his penis was normal because of the catheter. The next day, I took the cat to another facility, and they realized he was at risk of sepsis!!!! Not to mention the price, 900 euros for 2 nights, a catheter and making the situation worse!!!!

I brought my cat for a respiratory problem, and the first time I knew she'd be in good hands... but the second time I had confirmation that they're not only good vets but also good people.
The levels of empathy were extremely high. Dr. Aiello was a wonderful person, empathetic and understanding, but also very professional and attentive, especially to the cat. Dr. Ceccaroni was clear and gentle in communicating things. I regret not remembering the name of the doctor who helped me accompany my cat across the Rainbow Bridge. She was exceptional, patient, and comforting. It all happened very quickly.
But I'll never forget their attentive and reassuring looks, just as I'll never forget the smile of Elisa, the receptionist, who is always there to instill immense hope.
If you want your pets to be truly happy, even when things aren't going too well, this is the right clinic.
Zero professionalism.
Dr. Pavone was what I was looking for: professionalism, calm, a room where I could talk calmly, and empathy. Despite all the pain at the time, it was like breaking a sweat. Thank you 🙏🏻 …

I brought my cat in the middle of August for an emergency due to a side effect of an anesthesia administered at another facility. I met Dr. Arianna D'Arconte, and we immediately connected. She kept my cat under observation for at least half …

I brought my cat in for a urinary tract obstruction, he was admitted, and the problem was resolved.
The doctors were very good and very kind. They called me as soon as they had …

I'm not used to writing negative reviews, but I do it with the sole purpose of working on the staff, if possible. A month ago, my dog ​​fell ill and died at home. In a panic, I called the clinic in question, saying the dog had fallen ill …
Doctors Arianna and Valeria were very kind and very sweet with my cat who they visited late at night.
